items.text: Echoing Knocks
1921, Locker Room

items.speaker: Competitor I
items.text: Come on now; don't be nervous.

items.speaker: Competitor II
items.text: You can do this, you can do this!

items.speaker: Competitor III
items.text: Breathe in ... breathe out … breathe in ...
It's the moment before the finals. The preparation room is filled with anxious voices.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Everything alright?

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: I'm fine, Coach.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Sulis responded to my prayers again yesterday.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: And?
She looks at her intently.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: This time, she took me to the heart of a forest. The leaves there had spots all over them, like eyes. They were watching me, just like you are now, without blinking.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: I also heard a woman's voice. She was singing a slow song, something like ...

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: I can't quite remember the words.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: But I remember the rhythm.
She jumps up and moves in time to it.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Healing Sulis, shining Sulis, holy Sulis, to us, you tell.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Do you know it? The grass there sparkled. If I stayed too long on it, the little blades of grass would pinch me.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: All I could do was dance, dance, and keep dancing.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: So, I suppose witches weren't necessarily all burned at the stake. Maybe they just stepped on that kind of grass, you know?
She leaps high into the air and lands steadily.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Every time I jump, my shadowless friend lifts me just like this.
Energy flows around her, rustling her hair and leotard.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Keep dancing, just like this.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: If you make it to the end of this path, you'll snatch the sun right out of the sky.

items.speaker: Coach
items.text: Don't be nervous, Charlotte. Just treat it like any ordinary practice session.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: Nervous?
The girl looks at her palms to find a faint shimmer of sweat.

items.speaker: Charlotte
items.text: I'm not nervous, Coach.
She lifts her head and gazes at the sun shining in the distance.
That shining golden sun.
And behind it, those dark and boundless shadows.
*ring-ring-ring*
The doorbell interrupts her reminiscence.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You've got the day wrong, girl.
She hobbles to the door and opens it with force.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Today isn't snail day—

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What are you doing here?!
The visitor before her comes as a surprise.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Charlotte, I have some news I simply must tell you. You'll be utterly delighted to hear it, I'm sure.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: The Foundation has decided that they'll let you participate in the competition ... as a special athlete.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: You can return to the floor again!
She chatters on.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Get out!

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Oh, you want to know why?
She sneers through gritted teeth.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What is that you want? You wonder why I don't want to stroke your ego? To pump air into your already overinflated head?!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: You're just here to brag about your achievements!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Then, congratulations! You've done the job!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Are you satisfied, Caroline? I'm a cripple—a failure. Not your competition, but the object of your pity. That's what you wanted, right?

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: I'd never thought of it that way.
She wants to argue, but in this moment, a word of comfort cuts sharper than any blade.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: As if they'd invite me to perform in an "exhibition," like I'm some kind of monkey to be gawked at in a zoo. It's ridiculous!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Do I have to tell you it all, Caroline? How awful my life has been all these years? How people hate me? How my body has failed me?!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Does it satisfy your ego?

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I don't want to see you ever again!

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Charlotte!
A document falls to the ground. It bears the logo of the St. Pavlov Foundation.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: This is ...
She unfolds the document.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: "Regarding the Decision on the Participation of Ms. Charlotte O'Hagan ..."

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: "Upon careful consideration and evaluation, we hereby consent to Ms. Charlotte O'Hagan competing as a Floor Ritualist in the finals of the Uluru Games."

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What's the meaning of this?
She looks at Caroline in disbelief.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: Perhaps I didn't make myself clear, but ...

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: You're an athlete, not a performer. You won't be competing in an "exhibition." Nothing has changed, Charlotte.
Caroline holds Willow's trembling hands in her own.

items.speaker: Caroline Bartley
items.text: I look forward to seeing you on the floor.
